cues.text: Section twelve: Consolidation.
Let us pull the whole topic together.
Each area we have studied has a distinct job.
Governance sets direction and accountability.
Compliance establishes obligations.
Risk management prioritises uncertainty.
Security controls protect assets.
IT service management, or ITSM, delivers reliable services.
Change control protects stability during modification.
And finally, continuity and recovery protect critical operations during disruption.
Notice how these form a chain.
Governance says where the organisation is heading and who is answerable.
Compliance tells us what we are obliged to do.
Risk management helps us decide which uncertainties deserve attention first.
Security controls then defend the assets involved.
ITSM keeps services dependable day to day, change control keeps them stable when we alter them, and continuity and recovery keep critical operations going when disruption occurs.
Now a practical point for exams and for real work: use the framework that matches the question.
Each one has its own purpose.
COBIT is broad enterprise governance and management.
ISO 38500 is guidance for governing bodies.
ITIL is service management guidance.
ISO 27001 is a certifiable information security management system, or ISMS.
And ISO 20000-1 is certifiable service management.
Pay attention to two distinctions here.
First, ITIL is guidance, whereas ISO 20000-1 is the certifiable standard for service management.
Second, ISO 27001 is certifiable for information security management, while COBIT and ISO 38500 address governance, at the enterprise level and the governing-body level respectively.
Matching the framework to the question's focus is the key to choosing correctly.
